heuristics: The adding/squaring walk behaves as a random mapping on the prime-order group GT; the expected first-collision work is sqrt(pi*r/2) (standard Pollard-rho / van Oorschot-Wiener analysis), not a theorem for this specific partition.
The 80-bit distinguished-point predicate on canonical Fp12 encodings is close to uniform, so walk lengths and stored-record counts follow the stated geometric/birthday estimates.
A collision has different v coefficients with probability approximately 1-1/r; degenerate collisions are retried inside the charged expected work.
limitations: The claimed total is an expected Las Vegas cost, not a deterministic worst-case bound; all failures, restarts and detection delay are included.
Peak memory of about 2^57.5 bytes is analytically justified but astronomically large; memory is supplementary in this track.
No full-size execution is claimed; the toy experiment is evidence only at its stated scope.
Index-calculus attacks on the same GT discrete logarithm are not used or charged; this submission is not claimed to be the best-known attack.
The reduction is to the GT discrete logarithm with base e(P,Q0); no auxiliary powers are used and P is never replaced.
